method: Visually compared all listed source values, labels, headers and unit contexts with the existing source-page PNG renders and raw MinerU HTML. Each row expands to one annotation per value. Flags apply to each expanded annotation. Numeric correctness is distinct from usable structured-cell correctness. No source values are used by the prediction stage.

cvs_2025q2.note: All ten sampled cells retain the correct financial labels, periods and unit context.

rows.label: Revenue from sale of electricity and gas / Other revenues

edf_2024.note: MinerU joins three row labels and three unit strings into a shared cell. The first five numeric strings are right but lack a unique row/unit association. The next five concatenate values from two source rows, e.g. 3,037.10.0. These are association/merged-cell failures, not ten OCR digit errors.

hippodrome_2025.note: All ten sampled cells preserve their signs, financial rows, years and GBP units. Physical PDF page 20 has printed page number 18.

rolls_royce_2026h1_presentation.note: All ten sampled cells are correct. Organic change is not a simple subtraction of the two reported periods; no naive arithmetic rule is applied.

rolls_royce_2026h1_release.note: All ten numbers and row associations are right, but the primary export merges both period headers and units into a single colspan=3 cell. No unique per-column period binding is retained under this demo's strict structured-cell contract. This is unresolved header structure, not evidence that the numbers themselves are false.
